brief.title: PYPL Programming Language Popularity Index — April 2026
brief.one_liner: A data-driven snapshot of the world's most searched programming language tutorials, revealing Python's dominance and C/C++'s remarkable surge.
brief.goal: Viewers should understand which programming languages are trending up or down in 2026, grasp Python's commanding lead, recognize C/C++'s rapid growth, and note Java's continued decline — helping them make informed decisions about which languages to learn or adopt.

sections.title: Top 10 Languages by Search Share
sections.objective: Present the ranked table of the top 10 programming languages with their market share and year-over-year trend, making the hierarchy immediately visible.

sections.title: Biggest Gainers & Losers
sections.objective: Highlight the languages with the largest positive and negative shifts over the past year, emphasizing C/C++ (+6.2%), Python (+5.7%), Java (-5.4%), and JavaScript/C# (-3.0%).

sections.title: 5-Year Trend Spotlight
sections.objective: Summarize the longer-term trajectory: C/C++ grew the most over 5 years (+7.0%), Java lost the most (-7.0%), and Python solidified its #1 position.

sections.title: How PYPL Works
sections.objective: Briefly explain the methodology — Google Trends tutorial search analysis — so viewers understand the data source and its value as a leading indicator.

sections.title: Languages to Watch
sections.objective: Call attention to notable emerging or shifting languages outside the top 10, such as Ada (+1.1%), R (+1.6%), Julia (+0.4%), and Go's surprising decline (-1.3%).
